Forge & Hearth Retailers - Q2 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the Forge & Hearth Retailers Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Forge & Hearth Retailers's results for the Q2 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Michael Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Ruiz, Chief Merchandising Officer; Emily Patel, Chief Stores Officer; and Alex Rivera, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Michael Thompson.

Michael Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report Forge & Hearth Retailers's performance for the Q2 2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Today I will cover seven key aspects of our performance. First, comparable store sales grew 4.2% year-over-year, accelerating from Q1 and driven by traffic gains, higher average tickets, and strength in home furnishings. Second, supply chain efficiencies reduced costs by 17% as a percentage of sales, boosting inventory turns and margins. Third, omnichannel initiatives like BOPIS and curbside pickup saw 38% growth, now representing 22% of digital sales. Fourth, regional variations showed Sunbelt markets leading with 6.4% comps, while Northeast lagged due to weather. Fifth, we optimized our footprint with 12 new openings, 8 expansions, and 35 closures for a net reduction, enhancing sales per square foot. Sixth, our guidance assumptions include stable GDP growth, traffic up 1-2%, and margin expansion from private labels. Finally, Q3 comps are guided to 3-5%, with full-year sales up 6-8% and EPS at $4.65-$4.85.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more details on our financial results.

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Michael. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q2 2024.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.75 billion, a 5.2% increase compared to the same period last year, fueled by comp store growth and omnichannel momentum. Gross margin expanded to 28.4%, primarily driven by supply chain savings, lower markdowns, and a favorable mix shift toward high-margin private labels and home categories. Operating expenses were $640 million, representing 23.3% of revenue, with leverage from higher sales volume and productivity gains offsetting wage investments. Net income came in at $125 million, or $0.88 per share. We generated $260 million in cash flow from operations, supporting our remodel program and share repurchases. Inventory levels are currently well-controlled at 50 days on hand, with turns accelerating to 6.2x.

To give you deeper insight, let me start with comparable store sales—or comps—which remain the gold standard metric in our brick-and-mortar retail for gauging the health of our mature 1,200-plus store base, excluding new openings, closures, or major remodels. We're thrilled Q2 comps grew 4.2% year-over-year, our third straight quarter of positive growth and up from Q1's 2.8%, ahead of our flat to +3% guidance and topping the IDC-estimated 1.9% industry average for specialty hardlines and apparel. Traffic rose 1.5%, as shoppers returned to stores amid easing inflation. Average ticket climbed 2.6% to $78.42, with units per transaction up 1.2% and average unit retail up 1.4%. Conversion stayed steady at 28.4%, aligned with our five-year norm, thanks to better merchandising and staff training.

By category, home furnishings—42% of sales—posted 6.1% comps, powered by outdoor living like patio sets and grills amid warm weather. Apparel and accessories, 35% of mix, grew 2.8%, led by women's activewear and our private-label denim. Essentials and consumables, the stable 23%, edged up 0.3% as stocking normalized. Regionally, Sunbelt areas—Florida, Texas, Carolinas, 32% of stores—led at 6.4%, boosted by migration, job growth in logistics and construction, and 45 remodeled stores with interactive demos increasing dwell time 18%. Northeast and Midwest, 28% of footprint, managed 1.1%, hurt by wet weather impacting garden centers, much like Home Depot noted. California, 22% of sales, hit 3.7% with pricing discipline offsetting supply chain costs from regulations.

This reflects our Store 2.0 rollout in 320 stores or 27% of fleet, with BOPIS driving 28% YoY curbside growth and adding 1.2 points to comps. Salesforce Commerce Cloud partnership optimizes assortments by ZIP code, cutting markdowns 15 bps and lifting turns to 5.2x from 4.8x. Loyalty grew 12% to 14.7 million households, with members at +9.2% comps via personalized Forge Exclusive offers. Freight eased 8% YoY, shrink held at 1.6% with AI shelf-scanning in 150 stores. Q3 comps outlook is +3% to +5%, assuming steady sentiment, cooling CPI at 3.1%, wage gains, but watching Amazon and Wayfair in durables. These results affirm our physical retail strength blended with tech.

Building on that, our supply chain team delivered transformative efficiencies amid industry challenges like Red Sea issues, LA/Long Beach congestion, and earlier 20% freight hikes. We cut total supply chain costs 17% as a percentage of sales, from 8.2% to 6.8%, adding 220 bps to gross margins and dropping supply chain expenses 12% per store. Turns hit 6.8x from 5.1x, days on hand to 48 from 65, stockouts down 35% to 2.1%, contributing 150 bps to Q2's 4.2% comps.

This flows from our $250 million ChainForge initiative since FY2022, integrating automation, AI forecasting, and omnichannel across seven regional DCs and 15 micro-hubs. Autonomous mobile robots from Locus handle 65% of picking in four DCs, up from 15%, boosting throughput 40% to 1.2 million cases daily per DC. Blue Yonder AI cuts forecast error 28% to under 12% for high-velocity SKUs like apparel and hardlines, slashing markdowns 22% with just-in-time fills. In the U.S. (72% of stores), East Coast upgrades including a 1.2 million sq ft Sparks, Nevada facility mirror Home Depot's, hitting 98.5% on-time delivery despite port labor woes, aiding 5.1% Northeast/Midwest comps. Europe’s 180 stores onshored 40% apparel from Turkey/Morocco, trimming lead times to 28 days, saving €12 million. Asia-Pacific's 120 stores use RFID on 85% pallets, cutting shrink 18% amid disruptions.

These efficiencies fuel our moat: BOPIS capacity doubled to 25% of digital, store micro-centers handle 40% curbside, lifting traffic 8% and conversion 12%. Route optimization via FourKites cut truck miles 15%, reducing Scope 3 emissions.

Shifting to omnichannel progress amid inflation, down 2.3% YoY per NRF, and e-comm rivalry, these initiatives drive traffic and margins in our 1,200 stores. Omnichannel sales—digital fulfilled in stores—hit 22% of digital GMV, up from 16% YoY and 38% growth, beating e-comm comps of 15%. BOPIS jumped 45% to $285 million (18% digital orders), curbside Summit Express-style service up 52% to $210 million (14%). Like Target and Walmart, this boosts metrics: conversion 28% vs. 19% ship-home, via SummitSync OMS with Manhattan WMS, fulfillment under 2 hours in 85% stores, NPS 4.7/5. BOPIS AOV $145, 22% over ship-home, from pickup upsells like apparel bundles.

Northeast/Midwest (45% stores) topped 25% BOPIS penetration for urban needs; Philly micro-hub with Swisslog AutoStore does 15,000 picks daily, cutting labor 18%, same-hour curbside 70%. Sunbelt curbside grew 65% in Texas/Florida, ship-from-store fills 40% gaps at 98% in-stock with P&G/Levi's. SummitAI on Google Vertex predicts 92% accurately, RFID on 60% apparel cuts scan times 35%. Loyalty ties 65% transactions, 3.2x repeats, 28% bigger baskets, 15% win-backs via notifications. Traffic comped +4%, 35% BOPIS shoppers add 15 min browsing at 22% conversion, 250 bps margin lift from low shipping (1.2%) and returns (<5%). Targeting 25% penetration FY2025 with $100M for 20 micro-nodes, AR try-on.

On regional variations, while consolidated comps hit 3.2%, dispersion across Northeast (23%, 450 stores: +1.5%, flat traffic from rain, steady $48 basket, essentials up, apparel down, margins -40 bps to 28.9%); Midwest (28%, 550 stores: +2.9%, +1.2% traffic from low gas, $52 basket, pro sales up, margins +20 bps); South (30%, 600 stores: +6.4%, +4.1% traffic from migration/housing, $55 basket, home up 9%, omni 22%); West (19%, 370 stores: +1.8%, -0.8% traffic from fires/costs, $54 basket beauty strong, margins flat). Traffic +1.1% overall, conversion +15 bps via loyalty (65M members). Leaning CapEx 65% South/West remodels, rightsizing Northeast.

Regarding footprint, Q2 saw 12 greenfield openings, 8 relocations/expansions, 35 underperformer closures for net -15 stores, total now 1,156 across 48 states, 28.4M sq ft (-1.2% YoY), sales/sq ft $285 (+4.7%). New StyleHub small-box (15K sq ft) in Sunbelt/secondary markets emphasize BOPIS/AR; closures targeted low rent coverage/malls. Right-Sizing shuttered 112 past year, comps +2.8% vs. industry flat, productivity $425/sq ft. Sunbelt 65% openings, +5.1% comps; Rust Belt rationalizing. Future 15-20 net, micro-hubs near EV/logistics, ROIC 18.2% new vs. 7.4% closed.

For guidance assumptions, Q3 comps 3-5%, FY sales $10.4-10.6B (+6-8%), EBITDA $1.45-1.50B, EPS $4.65-4.85. Macros: GDP 1.8-2.2%, durable spend +2%, CPI 3-3.5%, unemployment 3.7-4%, mortgages 6.8-7.2%, freight flat. Traffic +1-2%, ticket +1.5-2.5% from private labels (18% sales), conversion 28-29% via kiosks, omni 22%, turns 5.2x. Margins +40-60 bps to 32.8% from markdowns/shrink, SG&A 22.5-22.8%, capex $850M. Sunbelt 5-7%, Northeast flat-+1.5%; intl stable. Horizon Forward: micro-DCs, Salesforce personalization, Rewards+ 45M, eco-lines.

Q3 sales $2.55-2.65B (+5-8%), comps 3-5%, margins 38.5-39%, EPS $1.25-1.35. FY comps 4-6%, margins 38.2-38.7%. Sunbelt 7%, Northeast flat-2%.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to David Ruiz, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, followed by Emily Patel to discuss store operations, and then Alex Rivera to discuss marketing initiatives.

David Ruiz, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Lisa. This quarter, we launched our Forge Exclusive rug and athleisure line, which has seen strong uptake with 6.1% category comps and outselling expectations in Sunbelt stores. We've optimized assortments using AI planograms, reducing markdowns and boosting high-margin SKUs. We are excited about the potential of this new product and other upcoming launches in outdoor living and private-label essentials.

Emily Patel, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, David. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented Store 2.0 enhancements including experiential zones and micro-fulfillment for BOPIS, now live in 27% of locations, driving 4% traffic comps and 18% dwell time gains. Positive results include higher conversion and ROIC on optimized footprint.

Alex Rivera, Chief Marketing Officer:
Thank you, Emily. Our Forge Rewards campaign has increased brand awareness by 20% and loyalty engagement, with 14.7 million members showing 9.2% higher comps through personalized offers. Digital integrations like app notifications boosted omnichannel repeats 3.2x.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your sales?

Michael Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Good morning, John. Inflation remains a headwind, with CPI ex-food/energy at 3.1%, but we've navigated it well through pricing discipline on high-margin SKUs, private-label expansion to 18% of sales priced 20-30% below brands, and value assortments. This supported 2.6% average ticket growth despite softer discretionary demand, as seen in flat essentials comps. Our middle-market focus—households $50K-$150K—benefits from 4% wage gains, and we've held promo rates to 18% of sales. Regionally, California managed 3.7% comps amid Prop 12 costs. Overall, it added stability, contributing to our outperformance vs. peers.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Sarah. For Q3, we're guiding comps to +3% to +5%, assuming stable consumer sentiment, 1-2% traffic from easier comps, 1.5-2.5% ticket from mix shifts, and steady 28-29% conversion. Tailwinds include cooling inflation and omnichannel lift—BOPIS/curbside adding ~1 point as in Q2. Sunbelt leads at low-double-digits on housing/migration, Northeast modest until holidays. Risks like higher unemployment could shave bps, but our loyalty and Store 2.0 penetration position us ahead of 1-2% industry.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson (Barclays):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Michael Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, Mike. Our ChainForge initiative yielded 17% cost cuts to 6.8% of sales, 6.8x turns, 48 days inventory, 2.1% stockouts. AMRs handle 65% picking, throughput +40%; AI forecasting error under 12%, markdowns -22%. New Sparks DC hits 98.5% on-time, Europe onshoring cut leads to 28 days, RFID slashed shrink 18%. This added 150 bps to comps, doubled BOPIS capacity, cut miles 15% for sustainability. Transformative for margins in this environment.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong (Morgan Stanley):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Michael Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Great question, Lisa. Our program grew 12% to 14.7 million active households, delivering +9.2% comps vs. non-members. In omnichannel, 65% transactions tie in, with 3.2x repeats, 28% larger baskets via personalized high-velocity offers. App notifications yield 15% win-backs, 2x redemptions like Ulta. Rewards+ targets 45M by year-end, 60% weekly engagement boosting traffic 4%, attach rates 15%. Key to our hybrid model.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Deutsche Bank. Please go ahead.

David Kim (Deutsche Bank):
Can you talk more about store openings and regional plans?

Emily Patel, Chief Stores Officer:
Thanks, David. Q2 net -15 stores to 1,156, but sales/sq ft +4.7% to $285. 12 new small-box StyleHubs in Sunbelt/secondary for experiential BOPIS/AR, 35 closures of low-performers/malls saved $42M. 65% CapEx to South/West remodels, 20 Northeast rightsizes to dark stores. FY 15-20 net micro-hubs near EV hubs, ROIC 18.2%. Aligns with migration, sustaining comps.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes the question-and-answer session.

Michael Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
